correctness.rationale: A bijection between distinct descendants and leftmost greedy embeddings gives a self-contained canonical-mask count. Alternating run compositions enumerate every fixed-weight word exactly once and mark the same cardinality. Hypergeometric local moments prove the mean; classical fixed-content runs CLT and O(n) variance for the local singleton statistic prove the n^(3/2) Gaussian limit. The actual included checker directly verifies all words at lengths 2..13 and formal products through 18. Finite computation is supporting evidence, not the proof.

evidence: A published unconditioned binary variance result gives Var(B)=(n-1)(n-2)(2n-3)/32. An accessible finite-alphabet complete-law claim likewise assumes independent uniform symbols and has no weight marker.
The fixed-length Levenshtein radius-one ball permits insertion after deletion, a different output relation.
Liron–Langberg arXiv:1202.1644 treats extremal descendant counts and per-run-type constraints, not the joint conditional ball-size law.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Conditioning on exactly k ones changes the joint distribution of adjacent transitions. The unconditioned law is only a binomially weighted mixture of conditional laws; it cannot determine all mixture components. The deterministic per-word identity permits brute-force enumeration but does not state or algebraically imply the coefficient formula and Gaussian scaling without new combinatorial/probabilistic work.

value.rationale: Fixed-composition inputs arise naturally in deletion-channel coding and sequence storage, and their without-replacement dependence differs substantially from iid inputs. The theorem gives a complete natural all-length histogram, a closed rational conditional mean, and a nontrivial density-dependent Gaussian fluctuation scale. The exact conditional array is not determined by its iid mixture, so it is a substantive reconstruction-capacity refinement rather than a textbook statistic. No larger-alphabet or more-deletion result is claimed.
